The geomagnetic Kp index measures Earth's magnetic field activity on a scale of 0–9. Kp 0-2 = quiet, 3-4 = moderate, 5-6 = geomagnetic storm, 7-9 = severe storm. At Kp 5+ auroras may be visible at lower latitudes.

Solar wind speed — a stream of charged particles from the Sun. Normal speed: 300–500 km/s. Above 600 km/s the probability of a geomagnetic storm increases significantly.

The southward component of the interplanetary magnetic field (IMF). When Bz is negative (pointing south), Earth's magnetic field opens and solar wind enters — the key trigger for auroras. Bz below -10 nT = strong activity.

The intensity of X-ray radiation from the Sun. Classes: A and B = quiet, C = moderate, M = strong, X = extreme. M and X class flares can cause radio blackouts and geomagnetic storms.
